newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank grants banking licence to local group.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank grants banking licence to local group.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it had granted a banking licence to a local consortium, AG Banka, which will take over the Slovak branch of troubled Czech bank Agrobanka.

NBS Banking Supervision Director Tibor Kasiak told Reuters the new bank -- with an initial basic capital of 500 million crowns -- will be fully-owned by oil and gas storage Nafta, drug makers Slovakofarma and Biotika, and pulp and paper maker SCP Ruzomberok.
"We issued the licence on April 14, but the final purchase of the Slovak Agrobanka (branch) is still subject to our final approval," Kasiak said.
Kasiak would not comment on the bank's shareholder structure.
The bank's balance sheet should be about five billion crowns.
The NBS had originally favoured a Slovak bank, not an industrial company, as a partner to start operating as an independent bank.
But, Kasiak said: "We, of course, tried to choose the best possible option...and the final choice was the best bid we received." He did not elaborate on other bids.
Slovak Agrobanka officials last autumn said the mother bank planned to transform its Slovak branch to a fully independent Slovak bank, in which Czech Agrobanka was supposed to have 34 percent stake.
But the original plan failed after the Czech central bank last September imposed forced administration on the Czech Agrobanka a.s..
